style: Say clearly and steadily, like a trusted radio news reader
ad_style: Say it like an excited TV ad announcer
lines: Here's an ad for a cereal called Zoom-O's. Tap Play ad and watch closely.
What did the ad want you to think? Tap a card.
Ads are all around us. Tap things you think are ads.
Who wants it? Count the hands, then tap Want it or Not sure.
Want it has forty votes. Tap Not sure, or tap a minus to correct a count.
Not sure has forty votes. Tap Want it, or tap a minus to correct a count.
Both counts are forty. Tap a minus to correct a count, or tap a part switch.
Now take a part out. Tap Music to turn it off, then play the ad again.
Only a plain bowl is left.
When did you want it most? What part was doing the selling?
Which part made you think that? Tap Music, Pictures or Words.
You found every ad here! Try another place.
Tap Play ad to watch this version.
The ad stopped. Tap Play ad to watch it from the start.
Tap another part to compare, or tap True? on a message card.
Music is off.
Music is back.
Pictures are off.
Pictures are back.
Words are off.
Words are back.
Tap Yes, start over to clear the votes, or tap Keep it.
It's the most fun
You get a toy
Everybody has it
It makes you strong
It tastes great
Cereal is food. The fun in the ad came from the music, the bouncing and the sparkles.
Some boxes have a small toy. The toy is not the cereal.
The ad says everybody loves it. Did the ad ask everybody? Ads say this to make you want to join in.
The ad never said that! Did you think it anyway? Pictures can make us think things nobody said.
Only a taste can tell you that. An ad can't.
The box itself is an ad. The mascot wants you to pick it.
Ads pop up in games.
Cartoons on food are there to catch kids' eyes.
It wants you to order pizza.
A menu tells you what's for lunch. It isn't selling anything.
A family photo helps us remember. It is not selling anything.
Ads ride on buses.
Billboards are big ads for people driving by.
A logo on a shirt is an ad you can wear.
It wants you to come in and buy.
A stop sign tells drivers to stop.
It tells us about a free story time.
Cereals for kids often sit low, right at kid eye level.
The mascot balloon wants you to notice the cereal.
Candy waits by the checkout, where kids wait too.
It wants you to buy two.
An aisle number helps us find our way.
It warns us the floor may be slippery.
NEW! Zoom-O's!
So crunchy! So fun!
Comet loves Zoom-O's!
Free toy inside!
Everybody loves Zoom-O's! Part of a happy breakfast!
